output.summary: KEP-3902 splits the taint-based eviction logic (TaintManager) out of NodeLifecycleController into a separate TaintEvictionController, so NodeLifecycleController only adds NoExecute taints and the eviction controller only deletes pods on NoExecute-tainted nodes. The KEP is implemented and at stable stage.
output.rationale:
NodeLifecycleController combined two independent functions: adding predefined NoExecute taints based on node conditions, and performing pod eviction on NoExecute taints. Splitting them is meant to disentangle the code and make future extensions to either component manageable. Reviewers agreed the refactor was a welcome cleanup, and the discussion narrowed the stated goal to code reorganization rather than enabling custom eviction controllers.</rationale>
<parameter name="outcome_reason">null

alternatives.why_not: The KEP says that keeping the code as-is "will make future extension of TaintManager harder and less flexible."

alternatives.option: Leverage existing tolerations for NoExecute taints to opt out of taint-based eviction
alternatives.why_not: The KEP lists disadvantages: it would require injecting tolerations into all pods via mutating webhooks or changing all workload manifests, still needs an extra controller to evict after coordinating with an external system, and webhook changes can conflict with default toleration admission and upgrades.

alternatives.option: Enhance the existing toleration APIs, e.g. a new EvictIfAllowed effect similar to PreferNoSchedule
alternatives.why_not: Listed as an alternative in the KEP discussion. The sources do not state a decisive reason it was rejected; the authors framed API extension as a larger change outside this KEP's goal.

evidence.quote: we propose to decouple `TaintManager` that performs taint-based pod eviction from `NodeLifecycleController` and make them two separate controllers
Splitting the `NodeLifecycleController` based on the above functionalities will help to disentangle code and make future extensions to either component manageable.
I don't see any problem with splitting the existing controller into two. This is a rather welcomed cleanup.
mostly LGTM. You should start requesting approval from SIG Node and PRR.
I think justification is more along the lines of cleaner design is better as we do not believe those scenarios are very important
